thread:
andrew: Quick heads-up: nightly perf showed a regression when using fused-RoPE + FlashA-v2 on seq=512. p50 jumped ~1.6x compared to yesterday.

maria: Ugh. numbers + repro command?

andrew: Pasted the quick snapshot:```
model: gpt-style-7b
cmd: ./bench --model gpt-7b --attn fused_rope_flash_v2 --seq 512 --batch 8 --runs 50
baseline (yesterday, flash_v1): p50=38ms p95=92ms tps=470
nightly (flash_v2+fused-rope): p50=62ms p95=210ms tps=310
GPU sm: 85% -> 92%
memcpy to device spikes during KV apply: +2.4ms/request
```

kevin: Hmm. kernel selector log? My gut: selector might be falling back to paged/fallback kernel because rotary dim alignment not supported by fused kernel. We saw similar when dims % 32 != 0. :eyes: 

sophia: Also check batching heuristic. If fused kernel increases per-request setup, continuous batching may pick larger batches that amplify memcpy.

andrew: Quick KV stats: cache hit rate steady ~98%. But profiler shows the hot path is KV copy + apply when using fused-rope. memcpy kernel occupies a lot more time.

raj: Could be layout: fused-RoPE expects interleaved rotary dims contiguous in memory. If our KV packing pads differently, the fused kernel does an extra tile-copy. Suggest two quick experiments: 1) force flash_v1 2) force kernel that assumes padded dims.

andrew: I ran the experiments: forcing flash_v1 drops p50 to ~40ms. Forcing "flash_paged_fallback" keeps it high. Disabling continuous batching (set max_batch=1) also reduces spikes. So there is an interaction between kernel choice and batching heuristic.

maria: Can you attach the kernel-selector trace? we need to know exact reason for fallback. I can add an assert in selector to log mismatch reasons.

andrew: Uploaded nvprof + selector trace to the artifacts bucket (artifact: nightly/1791234567/). Key lines: "kernel_selector: attempted fused_rope_flash_v2 -> rejected: rotary_dim_unaligned(30)"

kevin: Bingo. rotary_dim_unaligned(30). Our fused kernel requires rotary_dim % 32 == 0. Previously most models used 32/64 dims so it passed. New model variant uses 30 rotary dims due to pruning experiment. Kernel fallback triggers paged kernel which is memory-bound and loses batching benefits.

sophia: So options: 1) pad rotary dims at runtime/compile time 2) extend fused kernel to support non-multiple dims (costly) 3) change batching heuristic to avoid large batches when fallback happens.

raj: My preference: short-term pad to 32 (cheap, deterministic), medium-term add a tiled copy path in fused kernel that handles non-multiples without huge perf hit. Also add a selector metric that penalizes fallback heavy combos.

maria: I'll add a trace and quick fix to pad rotary dims in the model loader when fused_rope_flash selected. low-risk.

andrew: I'll open a repro PR with script that toggles rotary_dim and runs the bench matrix (seq128/256/512, batch 2/8/16). Attaching quick snippet to reproduce locally:```bash
# repro script
for dim in 30 32 48 64; do
  ./bench --model gpt-7b --rotary-dim $dim --attn fused_rope_flash_v2 --seq 512 --batch 8 --runs 30 
done
```

perf-bot: perf-alert: created issue perf/ropegap-1791234567; labels=[regression,attention,kv]

kevin: Follow-ups: 1) selector change to emit reasons when falling back (maria). 2) short-term pad in loader (maria). 3) batching heuristic guard: if selector indicates fallback, prefer smaller max_batch for seq>256 (I'll draft). 4) perf test to catch this in CI (andrew).

maria: Taking (1) and (2). Will send WIP PR by EOD.

sophia: Doc note: we should document fused-rope constraints and recommend rotary dim multiples for customers to avoid surprises in Dedicated/Private configs.

andrew: ack. I'll write the repro artifacts + upload profiler traces in the PR. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:

kevin: Nice triage. Once patch is up, let's run the nightly perf matrix and check p50/p95 for seq512 and the KV-copy counters.

andrew: Will run the matrix and post results here when done (ETA ~3h).

maria: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4123 (wip) -- includes selector logging + loader padding. Please review. :eyes:

andrew: quick follow-up after patch test: padding to 32 removed the regression in local runs: p50 -> 39ms. We'll still need longer-term kernel work but short-term is fixed.

sophia: :party-parrot: Great. Add a unit test to the kernel selector to cover rotary_dim variations.

kevin: Adding a CI perf job to run the repro matrix nightly for attention kernels. We'll watch for regressions.

andrew: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once nightly finishes and CI passes.
